A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same symbolic PDE recovery framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization and expanded experiments.

before.justification: Section 4 and Figure 2 report original numerical reconstructions of two linear PDEs from simulated incomplete, noisy measurements.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the linear-PDE experiments and reports original simulations and reconstruction results for seven nonlinear ODE systems and two 2D PDE systems.

M1.justification: The symbolic-network architecture, objective (Pm) and alternating optimization remain. Section 5.2.3 adds a constrained ParFam variant enforcing additive diffusion and excluding cross-terms between the Laplacian and state variables, a limited procedural extension.

E1.justification: Coverage expands from two linear 1D PDE examples to seven Strogatz ODE systems, the 2D Brusselator and a 2D membrane-transport system. These introduce coupled nonlinear dynamics, Laplacian-dependent laws, and polynomial, rational, trigonometric and exponential recovery tasks.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates separate competing recovery algorithms. The new comparisons vary ParFam architecture and structural constraints as ablations; cited approaches such as SINDy and EQL do not become evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce 10–80 ODE trajectories, system-specific architectures and optimization budgets, 64×64 and 32×32 PDE grids, and distinct measurement-resolution sweeps. They also introduce Savitzky–Golay derivative estimation and coefficient thresholding at 0.015 for error evaluation. These are additional protocols, not evidence that the original linear-PDE settings changed.

E4.justification: Beyond the original domain-dependent error analysis, v2 tests underspecified, default and extended architectures, and compares unconstrained recovery with additive diffusion constraints. Figures 3–7 also examine errors around trajectories and document difficult regimes, diffusion-coefficient recovery failures and variability across optimization runs.

E5.justification: v1 provides no repeated-run counts or uncertainty bands. v2 reports medians and interquartile ranges over 10 seeds for Figure 2, 15 seeds for the ODE experiments, and repeated-seed reporting for the 2D experiments. This establishes substantially stronger uncertainty reporting, without establishing how many runs underlay v1.

E6.justification: Figure 2 contains revised median curves, although the two displayed linear-PDE reconstruction formulas remain unchanged. Table 4 adds recovered ODE formulas and errors, including Lotka–Volterra errors of 0.14 and 0.11. Figures 4–7 add substantial PDE results, including unsuccessful diffusion recovery in the hard Brusselator regime and variable rational-term recovery in membrane transport.

T1.justification: The principal definitions, assumptions, reconstruction theorem, identifiability corollary and Appendix A–C proofs are retained after renumbering. However, v2 drops v1 Remark 8's assertion that the sampling operators satisfy condition (5) while failing the stronger convergence conditions discussed there, removing a limited mathematical assertion.

C1.justification: v1's abstract claims unique reconstruction of the simplest physical law. v2 instead states reconstruction of a representable, regularization-minimizing admissible law, with recovery of the unique true law requiring an additional identifiability condition. The conclusion likewise qualifies statements about network limits, substantially narrowing the headline guarantee to match the retained theory.

C2.justification: Section 4.1.2 substantially expands discussion of regularity, measurement injectivity and applicability beyond the earlier brief remarks. New experiments motivate explanations involving architectural misspecification, enlarged search spaces and local minima. The conclusion explicitly acknowledges limited numerical performance and distinguishes the analytical contribution from a mature numerical framework.

D1.justification: v2 adds substantial reproducibility information: early-stopping patience, regularization strength, derivative estimation, per-system architectures, restart and time budgets, forward solvers, grids and initial-condition generation. Tables 1, 3 and 6 organize these details. The documented code-access link also changes from an anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository.

R1.justification: Six references are added, covering transport regularity, operator learning, variational regularization and Lasso; the earlier cited works are retained. Section 1.2 sharpens the distinction from existing all-at-once frameworks and ParFam/EQL by emphasizing the nontrivial verification of symbolic networks' function-space properties.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially revised, related work becomes a separate section, and scope, novelty and organization receive dedicated subsections. Scattered assumption remarks become a structured discussion, and extensions receive their own subsection. This materially changes the narrative organization beyond simply inserting experiments.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 3–7 and Tables 1–6, introducing extensive multipanel results, architecture comparisons and configuration summaries. Figure 2 is redrawn with uncertainty bands and revised captions. Wider text blocks and changed typography also substantially alter the document layout.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's narrow validation on two linear examples through nonlinear ODE and 2D PDE experiments, architecture and structure tests, and explicit uncertainty reporting. Expanded implementation details improve reproducibility, while the abstract and conclusion better distinguish reconstruction from unique identification. The experiments still expose numerical failures, but reporting those failures and their variability makes the paper's practical scope considerably better supported.
